## CROP WEATHER WATCH GROUP (CWWG) MEETING HELD ON 03.02.2025

 

<!-- image -->
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

## Summary Points of the CWWG meeting:

## I. Preliminary Report of area coverage under Rabi season

## Rabi crops:

- - As on 31.01.2025 area sown under Rabi crops is 661.03 lakh ha as compared to 651.42 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
- - Sowing Status of Wheat: As on 31.01.2025, area of 324.88 lakh ha has been sown under wheat this year against the previous year area of 318.33 lakh ha while the normal area of wheat is 312.35 lakh ha.
- - Sowing status of Rapeseed & Mustard: As on 31.01.2025, an area of 89.30 lakh ha area has been sown under mustard against the previous year area of 91.83 lakh ha while the normal area under Mustard is 79.16 lakh ha.
- - Sowing status of Jowar: As on 31.01.2025, the area covered under Rabi Jowar is 24.35 lakh. Sowing is almost completed for the current season.

## Rabi Horticulture Crops :

- - For Onion, Potato and Tomato, an area sown has been reported by the major producing States, 9.62 lakh ha, 19.81 lakh ha, 2.15 lakh ha as against total sown area of 8.01 lakh ha, 19.49 lakh ha, 2.35 lakh ha, respectively in the last year.

## II. Weather:

- - Isolated light rainfall/snowfall is likely over the Western Himalayan Region on 3rd February 2025, with scattered to fairly widespread light to moderate rainfall/snowfall expected on 4th and 5th February under the influence of the second Western Disturbance (WD). A fresh WD is likely to affect Northwest India from 8th February, bringing isolated to scattered light to moderate rainfall/snowfall over the Western Himalayan Region on 8th and 9th February.
- - A gradual rise in minimum temperatures by 2-3°C is likely over the plains of Northwest India during the next 3-4 days and a similar rise is expected over Maharashtra in the next 2 days, with no significant change thereafter.
- - No significant change in minimum temperatures is expected over West and Central India during the next 24 hours, with a 2-3°C fall likely over these regions in the following 3 days.
- - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India and normal to above normal over northeast India during the week.

## III. Rainfall distribution:

- - All India seasonal cumulative (01st Jan 2025 - 03rd Feb 2025) rainfall in % departure from its Long Period Average (LPA) was (-)70%, with East & North East-India (-)49%, North-West India (-)79%, Central India (-)97% and South Peninsula (-)10%.

## IV. Water Reservoir Status:

- - As on 30th January, 2025, the total live water storage in 155 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 114.914 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 64% of total live storage capacity (180.85 BCM).
- - The current year's storage is nearly 121 percent of last year's storage and 116 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period.
- - The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

## V. Groundwater Levels Scenario

- - About 66.6% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 29.1% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. As per decadal water level fluctuation with a mean (August 2014 to 2023) and August 2024 analysis, 64.9% of monitoring wells (8199) show a rise whereas 35.1% (4435) show a fall in August month.

## VI. Seeds:

- - For Rabi 2024-25, availability of certified/ quality seed in the country is 337.98 lakh quintals against the requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals indicating an overall surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals of seeds.

## VII. Fertilizers:

- - Fertilizers position is stated to be comfortable in all products.

## VIII. Pests & Diseases:

Over all intensity of pests and disease remained below Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded.

Details of each sector have been enclosed at Annex.

## Rainfall Forecast:

## 30th Jan - 05th Feb 2025

- - Two fresh Western Disturbances are likely to affect Northwest India between 01st to 03rd February, 2025. Under the influence of these systems.
- - Scattered to fairly widespread light to moderate and isolated to scattered rainfall/snowfall activity likely over over Himachal Pradesh during 30th January05th February, Uttarakhand during 01st February-05th February and isolated to scattered light to moderate rainfall over Punjab, Haryana during 31st January05th February, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan during 03rd -05th February.
- - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India and normal to above normal over northeast India during the week.

## 06th Feb - 12th Feb 2025

- - No active western disturbance is likely to influence northwest India during the week. However, due to feeble Western disturbances, light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan Region during some/many days of the week.
- - Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is also likely over northeast India during some days of the week.
- - Under the influence of easterly winds from Bay of Bengal, isolated to scattered rainfall likely over South Peninsular & adjoining central India during some days of the week.
- - Overall, rainfall is likely to be normal to above normal over parts of central India and northeastern states; below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.

## Temperature Forecast:

## 30th Jan - 05th Feb 2025

- - Gradual rise in minimum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over the Northwest, East, Central and West India during 1st half of the week and no significant change thereafter.
- - No significant change in minimum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.

## 06th Feb - 12th Feb 2025

- - Minimum temperatures are likely to be between 4-8°C over Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh & Delhi and north Rajasthan and above 8°C over rest parts of the country during the week.
- - Minimum temperatures are likely to be near normal or slightly below normal by 1-2°C over most parts of the country during the week.
- - There is no probability of cold wave conditions over any part of the country and there is less probability of significant dense fog over any part of the country.

content.text: Summary Points of the CWWG meeting: I. Preliminary Report of area coverage under Rabi season Rabi crops: - As on 31.01.2025 area sown under Rabi crops is 661.03 lakh ha as compared to 651.42 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Sowing Status of Wheat: As on 31.01.2025, area of 324.88 lakh ha has been sown under wheat this year against the previous year area of 318.33 lakh ha while the normal area of wheat is 312.35 lakh ha. - Sowing status of Rapeseed & Mustard: As on 31.01.2025, an area of 89.30 lakh ha area has been sown under mustard against the previous year area of 91.83 lakh ha while the normal area under Mustard is 79.16 lakh ha. - Sowing status of Jowar: As on 31.01.2025, the area covered under Rabi Jowar is 24.35 lakh. Sowing is almost completed for the current season. Rabi Horticulture Crops : - For Onion, Potato and Tomato, an area sown has been reported by the major producing States, 9.62 lakh ha, 19.81 lakh ha, 2.15 lakh ha as against total sown area of 8.01 lakh ha, 19.49 lakh ha, 2.35 lakh ha, respectively in the last year. II. Weather: - Isolated light rainfall/snowfall is likely over the Western Himalayan Region on 3rd February 2025, with scattered to fairly widespread light to moderate rainfall/snowfall expected on 4th and 5th February under the influence of the second Western Disturbance (WD). A fresh WD is likely to affect Northwest India from 8th February, bringing isolated to scattered light to moderate rainfall/snowfall over the Western Himalayan Region on 8th and 9th February. - A gradual rise in minimum temperatures by 2-3°C is likely over the plains of Northwest India during the next 3-4 days and a similar rise is expected over Maharashtra in the next 2 days, with no significant change thereafter. - No significant change in minimum temperatures is expected over West and Central India during the next 24 hours, with a 2-3°C fall likely over these regions in the following 3 days. - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India and normal to above normal over northeast India during the week. Water Reservoir Status: - As on 30th January, 2025, the total live water storage in 155 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 114.914 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 64% of total live storage capacity (180.85 BCM). - The current year's storage is nearly 121 percent of last year's storage and 116 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. - The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. V. Groundwater Levels Scenario - About 66.6% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 29.1% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. As per decadal water level fluctuation with a mean (August 2014 to 2023) and August 2024 analysis, 64.9% of monitoring wells (8199) show a rise whereas 35.1% (4435) show a fall in August month. VI. Seeds: - For Rabi 2024-25, availability of certified/ quality seed in the country is 337.98 lakh quintals against the requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals indicating an overall surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals of seeds. VII. Fertilizers: - Fertilizers position is stated to be comfortable in all products. VIII. Pests & Diseases: Over all intensity of pests and disease remained below Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded. Details of each sector have been enclosed at Annex.

content.text: Rainfall Forecast: 30th Jan – 05th Feb 2025 - Two fresh Western Disturbances are likely to affect Northwest India between 01st to 03rd February, 2025. Under the influence of these systems. - Scattered to fairly widespread light to moderate and isolated to scattered rainfall/snowfall activity likely over over Himachal Pradesh during 30th January- 05th February, Uttarakhand during 01st February-05th February and isolated to scattered light to moderate rainfall over Punjab, Haryana during 31st January- 05th February, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan during 03rd -05th February. - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India and normal to above normal over northeast India during the week. 06th Feb – 12th Feb 2025 - No active western disturbance is likely to influence northwest India during the week. However, due to feeble Western disturbances, light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan Region during some/many days of the week. - Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is also likely over northeast India during some days of the week. - Under the influence of easterly winds from Bay of Bengal, isolated to scattered rainfall likely over South Peninsular & adjoining central India during some days of the week. - Overall, rainfall is likely to be normal to above normal over parts of central India and northeastern states; below normal over rest parts of the country during the week. Temperature Forecast: 30th Jan – 05th Feb 2025 - Gradual rise in minimum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over the Northwest, East, Central and West India during 1st half of the week and no significant change thereafter. - No significant change in minimum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. 06th Feb – 12th Feb 2025 - Minimum temperatures are likely to be between 4-8°C over Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh & Delhi and north Rajasthan and above 8°C over rest parts of the country during the week. - Minimum temperatures are likely to be near normal or slightly below normal by 1-2°C over most parts of the country during the week. - There is no probability of cold wave conditions over any part of the country and there is less probability of significant dense fog over any part of the country.
